acceptance_criteria.criterion: AC-1: no organization predicate means no rows, and the response never contains a profile email.
evidence: NO ORGANIZATION PREDICATE MEANS NO ROWS, and it is a query predicate rather than a post-read filter. The six `.in('id', chunk)` sites in app/api/tours/planner/artists/route.ts are: the roster id->user_id lookup (line 101), the `profiles` text-search leg (line 153), the direct `artist_profiles` read (line 172), the profile-matched `artist_profiles` read (line 200), the `profiles` enrichment (line 222) and the `artist_profiles` count (line 234). The count assertion is 6, not a lower bound, and a source test asserts exactly 6.

Fail-closed, with zero wide reads: an organization whose roster resolves to no artists returns `{ artists: [], total: 0, limit, offset }` and issues ZERO `artist_profiles` reads and ZERO `profiles` reads (test 'fails closed with an empty result and no artist read for an organization with no roster'). A roster lookup that ERRORS also resolves to an empty id set - `resolveOrgArtistRosterScope` ignores its own query errors and the scope resolver `continue`s past a failed chunk - so a broken roster is an empty scoped result, never an unscoped read.

The organization is structurally unreachable from the request. `org_id`, `ops_org_id` and `organizer_account_id` are rejected with 400 `organization_scope_field_rejected` before a single table is read (the test asserts `handlerReadsOn('artist_profiles')`, `handlerReadsOn('profiles')` and `handlerReadsOn('organizer_accounts')` are all empty for each of the three parameters). A spoofed `x-acting-org-id` header is refused earlier by the real resolver with 403 `acting_context_mismatch`, also before any read.

PROFILE EMAIL IS GONE, and asserted three independent ways. (1) Response: the serialized body is checked not to contain `ray@orga.test`, `vale@orga.test`, `cipher@orgb.test`, `outsider@platform.test`, `@orga.test`, or the substring `email`; `Object.keys(artists[0])` is pinned to the exact twelve-key list with no `contact`; `body.artists[0].contact` is asserted `undefined`. (2) Projection: every recorded `profiles` read's select list is split on commas and asserted to contain `id` and NOT to contain `email` - and the fake PROJECTS the requested columns, so a route that selected `email` would have it in the row and the assertion would have something to catch. (3) The projection constant itself lost the column: `PROFILE_FIELDS` is now `'id, username, full_name, name, bio, location, avatar_url'`, and the base source's `, email` is gone.

The `contact` object was removed rather than emptied. It only ever held `email: profile.email || null` and a hardcoded `phone: null`, and none of the four mounted consumers read it (checked individually: event-parties-panel mapArtist reads row.id/name/location; event-participants-tab mapArtist the same; app/admin/dashboard/events/create normalizeSelection reads a TOP-LEVEL `item.email` the route never returned; app/artist/events/create reads item.location/genre). The response is therefore a strict subset of the previous shape - every other field, the order, the limit clamp, the offset and the `total` are unchanged, and one test pins the whole authorized response value-for-value.

Base-SHA proof, not a claim: with the route replaced by `git show 16fb834f:app/api/tours/planner/artists/route.ts` (sha256 9ce05e579ba0b083c0c91b97cbd9b3d24a7cd14a9adcd3dde61ad9f501d290a0) the email-absence test fails on the real value - the base response body contains `"contact":{"email":"cipher@orgb.test","phone":null}` and `"email":"outsider@platform.test"`, i.e. another organization's private email and an unlinked platform user's, both verbatim. Restored byte-exactly afterwards.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: AC-2: a cross-tenant test proves a second organization receives zero artists.
evidence: __tests__/admin/tour-planner-artists-org-scope.test.ts, 19 tests, all green. The fake Supabase client HONOURS `eq` / `in` / `neq` / `or` (disjunction) / `contains` / `order` / `limit` / `range`, models `head: true` counts, and projects the requested columns - so a missing predicate produces a real cross-tenant result rather than an assumed one. `lib/auth/admin-context.ts` and `lib/admin/artist-roster-access.ts` are NOT mocked; only the transport is.

CROSS-TENANT DENIAL. 'returns nothing from another organization to an org A admin': an org A owner searching `nova` receives exactly [ARTIST_A1, ARTIST_A2] and the serialized body contains neither org B's `20000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000c` (Nova Cipher) nor the unlinked `...-00d` (Nova Outsider), nor the strings 'Nova Cipher' / 'Nova Outsider' / 'cipher@orgb.test'. 'returns an empty directory for a query only another organization matches, while its own artist still resolves' additionally shows a `cipher` query returns `{artists: [], total: 0, limit: 12, offset: 0}` while a `ray` query in the SAME test returns org A's own artist - so the empty result cannot come from a broken route.

NEGATIVE CONTROL A - the org predicate removed, observed red. All six `.in('id', chunk)` lines were deleted and the suite re-run: 10 of 19 failed. The core failure is the security claim, not a status code: 'returns nothing from another organization to an org A admin' failed with `expected [ ...(4) ] to deeply equal [ ...(2) ]`, received `["20000000-...-00c", "20000000-...-00d", "20000000-...-00a", "20000000-...-00b"]` - org B's artist AND the unlinked platform artist, in an org A admin's response. A `cipher` query returned that artist with total 1 where the repair returns an empty directory; the tour-collaborator test showed the same two extra ids; the count assertions showed total 4 where the repair shows 2, and 240 where the repair shows 120; and the AC-3 source test failed 'expected +0 to be 6'. Restored byte-exactly (sha256 0cfe43f0d1ba9ee60af228ea039d09035a404db7f919785685fd73443f69302e) and the suite returned to 19/19.

NEGATIVE CONTROL B - the base-SHA route over the new tests, observed red: 17 of 19 failed, with the same cross-tenant leak plus the four profile emails. The 2 that pass on base are the honest controls: 'still matches an artist through a profile field the artist row does not contain' (a `profiles.location`-only match, which the base's platform-wide search also finds - a no-widening regression control) and 'fails closed at the admin-surface gate before any organization work' (which depends only on the gate, so it must pass on both). This is the same shape as ADMIN-015's 9-fail / 7-pass split, and it means the suite is not satisfiable by the base behaviour.

ANTI-VACUITY (CP-098). 'delivers the acting organization its own roster artists' asserts 200, two named artists in order, and total 2 - on the SAME fixture and fake under which removing the predicate returns four artists. The denial is therefore demonstrably capable of returning rows; a plausible-but-false zero is not what this suite produces, and control A is where it produces one loudly. A second positive leg, 'still matches an artist through a profile field the artist row does not contain', seeds `profiles.location = 'Oslo'` on org A's first artist only and gets that artist back, which proves the profile-text search leg was scoped and not deleted.

The organization is read from the acting profile rather than a fixed id: with the session switched to org B's profile the same request returns org B's artist and none of org A's. Both fail-closed denials are tested against the real resolver, not a stub: 409 `acting_context_required` with no organization session, and 403 `organization_access_denied` when the user owns ORG_B rather than the acting ORG_A (the fixture deliberately makes them not the organizer-account owner so the resolver's owner fallback cannot rescue them), both with zero artist and zero profile reads.

The admin-surface gate is exercised, not stubbed: the `withAdminAuth` double delegates to the real `userHasAdminSurfaceAccess`, and the gate-denial test asserts the exact probe order `profiles, org_members, organizations, tour_team_members` so it cannot pass by short-circuiting.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: AC-3: the existing resolveOrgArtistRosterScope helper is reused rather than a second scoping rule being introduced.
evidence: There is exactly ONE call site: `app/api/tours/planner/artists/route.ts:96` reads `const roster = await resolveOrgArtistRosterScope(supabase, admin)`, imported from '@/lib/admin/artist-roster-access' at line 2, and its `artistProfileIds` are the only source of the `.in('id', ...)` scope on both tables. The whole helper is `resolveOrganizationArtistScope` (lines 76-108), whose job is to map that one roster onto the two id sets the queries need - `artist_profiles.id` and the matching `profiles.id` - and to return empty sets when the lookup fails.

NOT a second rule, asserted structurally: the file contains no `.from('organization_artist_members')` and no `.eq('ops_org_id'`, so the route cannot be hand-rolling the `organizer_accounts.ops_org_id` -> `organization_artist_members` chain that ADMIN-003 documented as the canonical owner of that concept. It also contains `resolveActingAdminContext` and no `searchParams.get('org`, so the organization cannot be sourced from the request.

NOT a second rule, asserted behaviourally: the recorded `organizer_accounts` read that carries an `ops_org_id` predicate is exactly one and its predicate is `['ops_org_id', ORG_A]`; the recorded `organization_artist_members` read carries `in('organizer_account_id', [PROFILE_A])` and `neq('status', 'removed')`. Those two recorded queries are the helper's own queries, produced by real code, which is what makes this a fact about execution rather than about the import line.

WHY THE HELPER FITS THIS SURFACE EXACTLY, which is the substantive part of AC-3: it returns `artistProfileIds`, i.e. `artist_profiles.id` values, and this route's row ids ARE `artist_profiles.id` - the value its four consumers persist as `artist_ids` into `event_participants.participant_id`. So the mapping is identity and needs no translation.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT COPIED, stated rather than hidden: ADMIN-015's route composes a SECOND leg (the organization's own `tours.org_id` -> `tour_artists.artist_user_id`) into a private `resolveOrganizationArtistUserIds` helper, because that route's ids are `profiles.id`. That leg is not reproduced here. Copying a private composition into a second file is exactly the failure mode AC-3 exists to prevent - two subtly different rules for one concept - and this route's ids are a different key, so the composition would not even be the same rule. The cost is real and is recorded as an accepted scope reduction plus a routed question: an organization can no longer discover, through this picker, an artist attached only to one of its tours and absent from its artist roster. The on-ramp is the org roster (`/api/admin/artists` POST invite/create, `/api/organization/artist-members`).

A SECOND THING DELIBERATELY NOT ADOPTED: ADMIN-015's `.eq('role', 'artist')` on its `profiles` read was already present on that route, so keeping it was a no-widening control. This route never had it, and adding it would be a narrowing unrelated to the organization boundary, so it was left off and the omission is recorded in the segment STATE.md rather than smuggled in.
